text: FII vs DII Investment Trends: What 10 Years of Market Data Tells FII and DII flows tell different stories about the same market. FII selling reflects global risk appetite, dollar strength, and emerging market allocation shifts, none of which are India-specific. DII buying, increasingly driven by SIP inflows that crossed ₹20,000 crore per month in FY24, reflects domestic retail confidence and a structural shift in Indian household savings from physical assets to financial assets. When FIIs sell, and DIIs absorb, market levels hold, but sector leadership changes. Export-linked sectors weaken. Domestically-oriented sectors, such as FMCG, banks, and infrastructure, tend to outperform. Your portfolio positioning should reflect which side of that trade you are on.
